highlights.text: Cetirizine also has anti-inflammatory properties and decreases production of prostaglandin D2 which plays a negative role in hair growth. So decreasing the production of PGD2 will help the patient.
highlights.comment: Awarded 1 mark for providing a clear pharmacological rationale explaining the mechanism of action (anti-inflammatory properties, PGD2 inhibition). This satisfies the 'pharmacological rationale explained for effectiveness' criterion.

highlights.text: It is said to be safe and has a lower potential side effect profile
highlights.comment: Awarded 1 mark for stating that safety risk is minimal with a lower side effect profile. This satisfies the 'safety risk is minimal' criterion.

highlights.text: results in improved compliance compared to other topical hair loss treatments
highlights.comment: Awarded 1 mark as an additional reasonable point regarding safety/efficacy - improved compliance compared to other treatments is a valid practical benefit. This satisfies the 'any other reasonable point regarding safety or efficacy' criterion.

highlights.text: Overall, the advantages outweighs its disadvantages but I would still look up more information, evidence and side effects on the hair restoring serum before putting in the pharmacy for sale.
highlights.comment: No additional marks awarded here. While showing critical thinking, this statement does not add new scorable content. Notably absent from the entire response: TGA approval status and listing on the register of therapeutic goods - these two criteria were not addressed at all, resulting in 2 marks being lost. Also, the rationale that cetirizine is already used orally by many people (supporting topical safety) was not explicitly mentioned.
